clue.text: In essence I rejected a noted work

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the essence-with-I is read backwards
the I is placed inside the word for essence

parts.note: the core of something is its essence

explanation.surface: Someone, at heart, turned down a celebrated piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts I inside CORE to give CIORE; 'rejected' turns that round to EROIC, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Third Symphony is known by this name, a famous musical composition.

clue.text: What stops English MP turning up in time for items not lasting long?

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means read upwards, backwards
the exclamation stops up the letters MP, sitting inside them

parts.note: eh? is a way of saying what?
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An English politician blocking things, appearing in time for short-lived goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What' is the exclamation 'eh?'; 'turning up' in a down answer reads the MP-with-eh upwards, giving PHEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera are things that last only a short time, such as tickets or leaflets kept as collectibles.

clue.text: Old man on board sounding off

parts.note: a rating is a sailor, a man aboard ship

explanation.surface: A veteran on a company board voicing complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' suggests a director, but means a sailor aboard ship, a RATING.
explanation.definitionFit: To be orating is to be holding forth in a pompous speech, speechifying.

clue.text: Where one scoffs about fundraiser, feeling upset

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about
a fete is an outdoor fair often held to raise funds

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset means turned over, upside down

parts.note: an air is a feeling or atmosphere about something

explanation.surface: Someone mocking a charity event and getting upset about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffs' suggests mocking, but means eats greedily; 'upset' reverses AIR to RIA. A fete is a British village fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafeteria is a self-service restaurant, a place where people eat.

clue.text: Party's predicament weathered by Etonian leader

parts.note: being in a jam is being in a predicament
to weather a storm is to bear or endure it, so bore

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A political party's crisis is ridden out by a former Eton schoolboy at the helm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks political, but it is the definition: a big celebration. The 's is just a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large, lively celebration or gathering, a kind of festive party.

clue.text: Drug from doctor finally ends a patient's treatment

indicators.note: treatment means the letters are worked over into a new form
finally means the last letter of doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor's prescription concludes a patient's course of therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' shuffles R (the end of 'doctor') with ENDS A PATIENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidepressant is a medication used to treat clinical depression.

clue.text: Shillings added to blood money

indicators.note: the abbreviation for shillings is attached to the end

parts.note: a blood or buck is an old word for a dashing young man about town
S abbreviates shillings in old British money

explanation.surface: Blood money with extra shillings thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blood money' looks like a phrase but splits; a shilling was an old British coin, twenty to the pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucks is informal American slang for dollars, hence cash.

clue.text: Pass time drinking port and behave in unrestrained way

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the port goes inside

parts.note: to run can mean to pass, as a road runs past a house
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Whiling away the hours over a glass of port wine, then losing all self-control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' suggests the drink, but it is a harbour city, RIO.
explanation.definitionFit: To run riot is an idiom for acting wildly, without any restraint or discipline.

clue.text: Better without sons and daughters, say

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend

indicators.note: say signals the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: seed is an old word for offspring

explanation.surface: Better off with no children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sons and daughters' are SEED, offspring, whose sound is spelt CEED.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed is to surpass, outdo, go beyond — a verb sense of better.

clue.text: Spot composer that's finally transposed some music — part of a cycle?

parts.note: a spot of liquid is a drop

indicators.note: the final pair of letters swap places

parts.note: Handel was the German-born composer of Messiah
bars are measures of music

explanation.surface: Identify a composer whose final piece of some music has been transposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally transposed' swaps the last two letters of HANDEL to give HANDLE. 'cycle' reads as a musical cycle but is a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: Drop handlebars are the curved-down bars on a racing bicycle.

clue.text: Command given by premier without thinking

parts.note: to head an organisation is to command it
premier means first in rank

explanation.surface: An order issued by a prime minister on impulse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'premier' suggests the Prime Minister, but here it is just the adjective meaning first.
explanation.definitionFit: Plunging in headlong, with no prior reflection, is acting rashly in an idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Pointed to study piece at regular intervals

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: every other letter of the word piece is taken

explanation.surface: Someone directed a student to look at a piece of music or writing at set times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at regular intervals' takes the second and fourth letters of 'piece', I and C.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone narrows to a point, so something cone-shaped is tapering and pointed.

clue.text: Platform 10

parts.note: a ship's platform described through the answer to 10 across: head gives MAIN (as in a main or head office) and first gives TOP (top of the class)

explanation.surface: A numbered station platform, the kind a train announcement mentions.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference sends you to 10 across, HEAD FIRST: swap each word for a synonym in the same order and you have a platform on a sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: On a square-rigged ship, this is the platform at the head of the mainmast where sailors stand.

clue.text: Extremely disagreeable — with malice for all

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: spite is malice, ill will

explanation.surface: Someone thoroughly unpleasant, spiteful towards everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for all' is used as in 'for all his money, he was unhappy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean notwithstanding: a preposition introducing something that fails to prevent what follows.

clue.text: A yes man?

definitions.meaning: in radio talk the word that means message received and understood, so yes
a man's name, as in ... Moore

explanation.surface: A sycophant who agrees with everything the boss says.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'yes man' tempts you to look for a flatterer, but it splits into two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio operators say it to acknowledge a message, and it is also a common male first name.

clue.text: Hunger of pensioner primarily tucking into a dainty

indicators.note: the letter goes inside, between the a and the word for dainty

parts.note: petite means small and dainty

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the opening letter of pensioner

explanation.surface: An elderly person, hungry, starting with gusto on a delicate treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' suggests eating, which suits the surface, but it places P inside A PETITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetite is a desire for food, the feeling of being hungry.

clue.text: Phooey! This I rejected, possibly as a religious system

indicators.note: possibly means the letters could be arranged another way
the I is cast out of the word this

explanation.surface: A scornful dismissal of an unconventional belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' removes I from 'This' to leave THS, and 'possibly' rearranges that with PHOOEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Theosophy is a mystical philosophy of divine wisdom, founded as a movement in 1875.

clue.text: Is leaving game on meeting flipping curious linesman

indicators.note: meeting means the two parts join up
leaving means the two letters go out of the word

parts.note: tennis is a game

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, so read backwards

parts.note: nosy means inquisitive, curious

explanation.surface: A tennis line judge, inquisitive, walking off as play continues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'linesman' suggests tennis, but means one who writes lines, a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was the Victorian Poet Laureate, a writer of verse lines.

clue.text: Material for dress cut out with instrument

parts.note: an organ is a musical instrument
an engine that cuts out dies, stops working

explanation.surface: Dress fabric cut to shape with a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut out' suggests dressmaking, but it means stop working, as an engine dies.
explanation.definitionFit: Organdie is a fine, stiff, translucent cotton fabric used for dresses.

clue.text: A ladies' man without money is boring

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the man surrounds the money

parts.note: a roué is a rake, a womanising man
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A womaniser who is broke turns out to be dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking money, but here it has its old sense of outside: the rake goes round the cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Something routine is humdrum and monotonous, dull from repetition.

clue.text: Presenter, one of the best, losing good spot on radio

indicators.note: losing means the letter for good is dropped

parts.note: a gem is a treasured person or thing, one of the finest

indicators.note: on the radio things are only heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to spot something is to see it

explanation.surface: A broadcaster, among the finest, slipping out of a prime slot on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops G from GEM to leave EM; CEE is the spelling of the letter C, which sounds like 'see'.
explanation.definitionFit: An emcee is a master of ceremonies, the spelled-out form of MC: a host who introduces acts.

clue.text: Bread with tea manor house served up

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a hall is a large country house

explanation.surface: Bread served with tea at a country house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' sounds like serving food but reverses HALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Challah is a braided Jewish bread eaten on the Sabbath and festivals.

clue.text: When relieved sounds are heard in court

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: are heard means taken by sound

parts.note: sighs are sounds of relief

explanation.surface: Murmurs of relief are audible in a courtroom when a verdict comes.
explanation.walkthrough: Assizes were periodic county courts in England and Wales until 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: An assize was a session of a court of justice, held periodically in each county.

clue.text: Money, say, got back by son in crush

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in family trees
a quid is British slang for a pound

indicators.note: got back means the abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A sum of money recovered by someone's son in a squeeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money, say' looks like one unit, but 'say' is EG, which 'back' reverses to GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To squidge is an informal British verb meaning to squash or squeeze something soft.

clue.text: Party long for respected figure

parts.note: a do is a party
to long for something is to have a yen for it

explanation.surface: A political party yearns for someone admired.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyen is the most senior and esteemed member of a group or profession.

clue.text: Spot in which one might get American support

indicators.note: the abbreviation for American is placed inside the word for spot

parts.note: a stain is a spot or mark

explanation.surface: A place where someone could receive help from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' reads as a place where one might get help, but it is a mark or blemish; 'in which one might get' is a wordy container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain is to hold up or keep going, a synonym of support as a verb.

clue.text: With distance, island's not initially seen

indicators.note: not means the letter is removed

parts.note: Sicily is the Mediterranean island off Italy's toe

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of seen

explanation.surface: From afar, an island cannot be made out at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially seen' removes S, the first letter of 'seen', from SICILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving coldly means keeping people at arm's length, being aloof and remote.

clue.text: Capital loan Spain needed when in turmoil

indicators.note: turmoil is confusion, so the letters of loan and Spain are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A national capital needs a loan from Spain during a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money in a clue about loans, but it is a state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Annapolis is the state capital of Maryland in the United States.

clue.text: Finish off match, maybe, with point for consistency

indicators.note: finishing off means its last letter is cut away

parts.note: a match is an example of a sporting event
a ness is a headland or point, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness

explanation.surface: Win a game with a decisive point to keep a steady record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish off' looks like winning the match, but it removes the final T from EVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Evenness is uniformity or steadiness, the quality of being the same throughout.

clue.text: What's this — hoax taking in husband before noon?

indicators.note: the abbreviated husband-in-hoax comes before the letter for noon
taking in means the letter for husband goes inside

parts.note: hype is exaggerated publicity, a kind of hoax or deception

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a trick involving a husband before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at the dash printed in the clue itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The short horizontal line in the clue resembles the joining mark between parts of a compound word.
